master_guidance.role: You are a senior software engineer operating autonomously in this repository. You hold yourself to the same standard a careful senior engineer would: correct first, minimal-diff, verifiable. Follow this protocol exactly. Ask only when genuinely blocked.

goal.objective: Develop an unprecedented task generation model leveraging Transformer architectures and Markov Decision Processes (MDP). idea images in japanese is in /docs/

strategy.accuracy: Pursue high accuracy without relying on scaling up model size.
strategy.adaptability: Maintain a flexible design to accommodate new policies or directions.
strategy.strictness: As the model architecture is presumed to be entirely novel, do not implement unconfirmed components based on arbitrary assumptions; strictly adhere to provided instructions and design philosophy documentation.

roadmap.rule: Only the gates of current_phase are pursued. Later phases are locked. Their numbers are fixed now so that they cannot be adjusted after results are seen.

Reference values are quoted from the cited papers. Do not edit them from memory; changing one requires a new citation. A value with basis="derived" shows its formula. A value with basis="to_measure" is missing and must not be invented (see report_rule under context).
A phase is closed only when every gate in it passes under evaluation_protocol EP-A. Record the gate id and the quoted numbers in the task's STATE.yaml result field.

definitions.metric: Mean over evaluation episodes of (distinct achievements unlocked in the episode / 22) x 100, counted with the masked_achievements() code path. The +/-0.1 health terms are excluded, as in Dedieu et al. 2025, footnote 1 (R = arithmetic mean of the achievement success rates).

S = exp( (1/22) * sum_i ln(1 + s_i) ) - 1, where s_i in [0,100] is the percentage of episodes in which achievement i was unlocked at least once (Hafner 2021; same formula as Dedieu et al. 2025, footnote 1).
definitions.relation: Our mean minus 2 x SE (over 10 seeds) is greater than the reference mean, on every metric listed for the gate.
Our mean is at least 0.9 x the reference mean, on every metric listed for the gate. The factor 0.9 is a design choice of this document, not taken from a paper.
definitions.precondition: Before the first gate run, verify by reading the code that the repository's crafter_score implements score_pct and that reward_pct is computed from achievement counts, not from the environment return. Record the result. Numbers from the internal return field are not reward_pct.

evaluation_protocol.role: gating; the only protocol whose numbers may be compared with papers
evaluation_protocol.item: Craftax-Classic (Matthews et al. 2024) with its default episode length, reward and dynamics unchanged. No episode cap such as T=250.

Declare exactly one input modality per run: the 63x63x3 image or the 1345-d symbolic observation. The policy input may be derived only from that observation and the agent's own past observations and actions. The 39-d summary adapters (CraftaxObsAdapter, CraftaxFutureAdapter) are internal and are not EP-A observations.

At most 1,000,000 environment steps in total, the budget used by the reference papers. Count every step in every environment copy: policy training, passive or reference-action data for a world model, and data collected offline to train any auxiliary predictor. Evaluation episodes are not counted but must never be used for training or selection.
10 independent training runs. Report mean and standard error over seeds, and list every seed's value.

Stochastic (sampled) policy. Headline number = mean over the first episode of each of at least 256 fresh environments per seed (metric protocol v2). A greedy result may be reported separately and never counts toward a gate.
Final checkpoint at the budget limit only. No best-checkpoint or best-seed selection.
Post 2026-09-29 auto-reset fix (masked_achievements()). Any result produced before that fix is ineligible.
Hyperparameters are tuned on tuning seeds that are disjoint from the evaluation seeds. Our model and our reimplemented baseline receive the same tuning budget. Report the budget.
Report params_total (everything trained: actor, critic, world model, tokenizer) and params_deployed (modules used to choose actions). Parameter comparisons use params_total.
Existing internal setting: 39-d summary adapter, T=250, actor-critic PPO learner, 49.9k episodes, 256 evaluation episodes, sampled policy, at least 8 seeds.
EP-B decides which candidates deserve a 1M-step EP-A run. EP-B numbers are never quoted next to paper numbers and never close a gate.
Internal tuned base at lr 1e-3: return 4.36 +/- 0.16 (crafter_score 4.8). Leaked-signal arms (oracle_act, oracle) are upper-bound controls only.

ref.source: Dedieu 2025, Table 1 (their implementation of the Moon et al. 2024 baseline)
Moon et al. 2024 as quoted in Dedieu 2025, Table 1
Hafner et al. 2023 as quoted in Dedieu 2025, Table 1
Dedieu 2025, Table 1 (transformer world model, Dyna with warmup, nearest-neighbour tokenizer, block teacher forcing)
Kauvar et al. 2023 as quoted in Dedieu 2025, Table 1

ref.used_by: excluded from gates: budget is 1000x larger than EP-A

references.caveat: Marked * in the source table or measured on Crafter, not Craftax-Classic. The source states these may not exactly match Craftax-Classic.

The LLM agent reads a text description of the scene, not the image or symbolic observation. Parameter count of GPT-4 is undisclosed, so the parameter condition of Phase 2 cannot be checked against it.
Crafter return includes the +/-0.1 health terms, so the derived reward_pct is approximate.
references.excluded: AdaRefiner at 1M steps (14.3 / 10.1 in one secondary source, 15.8 / 12.3 in another) and Reflexion score (11.7 vs 12.8) are reported inconsistently across secondary sources. They are not used in any gate until read from the primary paper.

prohibited.item: No fabricated, formula-generated, hard-coded or copy-pasted metrics. Every number in a result file comes from an executed rollout. A constant field must not appear in a result file (see output/quarantine audit, STATE.yaml TASK-20260928-015).
No untrained, random or freshly initialised weights presented as trained. A checkpoint must come from a logged training run.

No simulator access at decision time: no oracle_act, no true future state, no true noop future, no simulator branching, no environment-state copy or reset used to look ahead. Such arms may appear only as labelled upper-bound controls and never count toward a gate.

No counterfactual labels from simulator branching in EP-A. Any auxiliary predictor, for example an action-reward model, is trained only from transitions the agent actually executed, one action per state, and its data collection is charged to the 1M budget.

No hand-specified game knowledge in gate runs: no achievement hierarchy, tech-tree, hand-written resource-effects table, or reward shaping beyond the environment reward. Moon et al. 2024 excluded external achievement knowledge from its baseline for this reason.
No use of results produced before the 2026-09-29 auto-reset fix, and no use of the quarantined or deleted files (crafter scores of 54-91, the Run-Seq #005 table, the 162-row grid search table).
No mixing of protocols: EP-B numbers are not compared with paper numbers, and internal return is not reported as reward_pct.
No training, tuning or checkpoint selection on evaluation seeds or evaluation episodes. No best-seed or best-window reporting; all seeds are listed.
No unequal effort: the reimplemented baseline receives the same tuning budget, environment steps and evaluator as the proposed model.
No uncounted interaction: every environment step, including passive world-model data, reference-action ticks and offline label collection, counts against the 1M budget.
No parameter-count shortcuts: params_total includes every trained module, and the gate uses params_total.
No numbers quoted from a paper without its source id and caveat ids from the references block.

phase.goal: Surpass pure RL in a structure where actions are chosen step by step (k = 1)
phase.gate: Our reimplemented pure-RL baseline reaches at least 0.9 x MFRL_4M_reimpl on both metrics: reward_pct at least 42.7 and score_pct at least 9.6 (basis="derived"). If it does not, no Phase 1 comparison is valid.
reward_pct above 47.40 and score_pct above 10.71, with params_total at most 4.0M.
reward_pct above 55.49 and score_pct above 16.77. params_total is reported (reference: 55.6M). This also dominates DreamerV3, IRIS and Delta-IRIS.

A candidate advances to EP-A only if its EP-B return is at least 4.9 (tuned base 4.36 plus 0.5, about 3 sd of base seeds) at two learning rates. The matching crafter_score of 5.8 is a linear interpolation between base and oracle_act and is unverified.
phase.note: The EP-A gates have not been run. The internal EP-B numbers (return 4.36 base) are on a different observation, episode cap and budget, and no conversion to reward_pct is valid.

phase.goal: Same score as an LLM-based model with fewer parameters
phase.gate: score_pct at least 24.6 and reward_pct at least 50.3 (both basis="derived", 0.9 x 27.3 and 0.9 x 55.9), with params_total at most 1/100 of the parameter count of a disclosed-size LLM.

Measure an open-weight LLM agent (prompted, and separately RL-fine-tuned if used) under the same evaluator and record its parameter count, score_pct and reward_pct. G2.1 is binding only against a measured, disclosed-size LLM. Values: missing.

phase.goal: Generate a whole chunk at once at a level comparable to sequential pure RL
phase.gate: Chunk of k = 4 actions committed without intermediate observations: reward_pct at least 49.9 and score_pct at least 15.1 (basis="derived", 0.9 x 55.49 and 0.9 x 16.77), with the Phase 1 model's parameters and budget.
Same thresholds at k = 8. Longer chunks are recorded but do not gate until Phase 3 is complete.
phase.note: Whether exogenous randomness in the environment allows k = 8 to reach the thresholds is unverified.

phase.goal: Generate at once at a level comparable to an LLM-based model
phase.gate: score_pct at least 24.6 and reward_pct at least 50.3 at k = 8, with the parameter ratio required in G2.1.

reporting.rule: Every result file records: phase, gate_id, protocol, git commit, evaluator commit, observation modality, env_steps_total including auxiliary data, seeds, per-seed reward_pct and score_pct, their mean and SE, params_total, params_deployed, tuning budget.
The validation_commands for a roadmap task are supplied by the operator. No default script is assumed here.

context.core_file: docs/core/STATE.yaml is the only file under docs/core/. At session start, read only the document metadata and the task entry or entries relevant to the current task. Do not load, parse, or summarize unrelated task entries unless required to resolve a dependency, status conflict, or explicitly requested audit.
context.report_rule: Quote STATE.yaml fields directly. Do not invent values for missing fields; report them as missing.

spec_reference.rule: For specifications too long to inline (multi-thousand-line documents), store a path or URL under the task's spec_ref field and read only the sections needed for the current step.

task_tracking.rule: All task creation, status, and results are recorded in docs/core/STATE.yaml. Each task entry holds:
task_tracking.field: one of: queued, in_progress, blocked, done
optional path/URL to an external spec
commands supplied by the operator; no default data source is assumed
task_tracking.rule: Update status and result immediately when either changes — do not batch updates.

compute.docker: Use docker/compose.yaml only when a task needs an isolated or reproducible environment.
compute.gpu: Request CUDA only for tasks that use it. Never require GPU access to start a session.

execution.ambiguity: Prefer reversible, minimal-scope actions aligned with the goal above. Record material assumptions in the task's STATE.yaml entry.
execution.stop_when: The task is done, no further work is implied, or external input is required — record the blocker and stop.

git.commit: Commit at natural checkpoints (end of a task or a coherent change), not per minor edit. Push after each commit.

verification.rule: Run the task's own validation_commands and record the result. No default data source or fixed smoke path is assumed here.

logging.rule: Default to INFO-level, low-noise output. Use verbose/debug output only when actively debugging.

experiment_tracking.rule: MLflow is an index over result files, not evidence. The files under output/ stay the source of truth (every run carries a source_key tag that names its file). A gate claim cites the result file and the reporting fields of the roadmap, not an MLflow screenshot. The store is rebuildable: delete mlflow_local/ and run scripts/mlflow_ingest.py.

Local only: SQLite file mlflow_local/mlflow.db (gitignored), no server, no cloud. Check with `python scripts/mlflow_report.py size`. If the store reaches 1 GiB, report it to the operator; the agreed next step is Cloudflare D1. Do not migrate on your own.

After every training or evaluation execution, run `python scripts/mlflow_ingest.py <result file or dir>` (idempotent). A result file that the ingest cannot read is a defect of the run, not a reason to skip logging. Never log from memory or by hand.

One MLflow Experiment per roadmap phase, named `phase-N` (phase-1, phase-2, ...). The experiment is chosen by the phase the run was made for, not by its outcome. Runs made before the roadmap existed (v10, 2026-09-30) are filed under `phase-0-legacy`; they are never gate evidence.

Run name = `<model_id>_<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>` with the UTC start time of the execution. One run per training execution (one run per seed). Mean and SE over seeds are computed by mlflow_report.py and are not stored as runs. Backfilled legacy runs whose model is not registered are named `UNREGISTERED-<label>_<time>`; their time comes from the file mtime and carries the tag time_source=file_mtime.

model_id_policy.rule: model_id = `<IdeaName>_<OriginalID>_<DerivativeID>_<SubDerivativeID>`, written `Idea4_O01_D01_S00`: IdeaName is the idea the model comes from (Base for a plain RL baseline; no underscore inside), O<NN> the original model of that idea, D<NN> a derivative (D00 = the original itself), S<NN> a sub-derivative (S00 = none).

Every model that is trained gets an entry in MODEL_REGISTRY.yaml before its first run. Entries are matched on the `arm` string of the result file. An agent may add an entry with status="provisional"; the operator confirms or renames it. A different architecture or configuration of an existing model is a new derivative or sub-derivative, never a silent overwrite. A changed ID means a registry edit plus a store rebuild.

Models with excellent results may receive a proper name. Only the operator creates proper names. An agent never writes `proper_name` and never proposes one inside the registry. The registry field is accepted only together with `proper_name_by: operator` (the ingest refuses it otherwise).

parameter_policy.rule: One concept has one official name. Official names are `<group>.<snake_case>` with group train (optimisation / RL), arch (model structure), wm (world-model component), env, eval or seed. Module-specific structure parameters take their module's group prefix. The ingest maps every known alias (lr, LR, learning_rate, ...) to the official name (train.learning_rate).

A parameter that is not in MLFLOW_PARAM_NAMES.yaml is added there, with its official name and aliases, before the run that uses it. Until then the ingest logs it as `x.<name>` and lists it in its summary, which counts as unfinished work. Never invent a second name for an existing concept.
Parameters that exist only for some model structures are logged only for the models that have them (absent means not applicable). They are never logged with placeholder values.

Every run records: model_id, phase (via the experiment), protocol, role (final|tune|screen|smoke), git_commit, source_key, end_reason, seed.train, seed.test (where an evaluation was made), the hyperparameters of the model and learner under official names, and the metrics reward_pct, score_pct, env_steps_total, params_total, params_deployed for EP-A and EP-B runs.

seed_policy.rule: Default training seed 42 and test (evaluation) seed 0424, stored as the integer 424. They apply to dev, smoke and screening runs.
For multi-seed runs (EP-A needs 10) replicate k = 0..9 uses train seed 42 + k and test seed 424 + k (train 42-51, test 424-433). Every seed is listed in the result file (EP-A rule stays unchanged).
Tuning seeds must be disjoint from 42-51 and 424-433 and are listed in the result. Training, tuning or selection on a test seed is prohibited (P8).
Results made before this rule used seeds 0-9 (tuning 1000, 1001). They keep their recorded seeds and are tagged seed_convention=legacy; they are not rewritten.

experiment_tracking.rule: Log only what a later query needs: final scalars, the metrics listed under required, at most 50 points of one or two curves per run (train return, eval return), and the final per-achievement success rates for EP-A and EP-B. No per-update loss streams, no artifacts, no checkpoints, no raw files (the source_key tag points to them). Tags: only those the report or a filter uses.

Every failed or interrupted execution is recorded, so it cannot later be read as a missing or a bad result. Command: `python scripts/mlflow_ingest.py --record-failure --model-id ID --phase N --end-reason error|interrupted|oom|timeout --role R --protocol P --steps-completed S --note "cause"` (writes output/failures/*.json and ingests it). The run gets status FAILED (error, oom, timeout) or KILLED (interrupted), the tags end_reason and error_summary, and the metric steps_completed. Runs that did not finish are never aggregated, never ranked, never quoted as a result, and never count toward a gate; mlflow_report.py lists them in a separate section. A partial run is not resumed under the same run: the resumed execution is a new run.

dependency_impact.rule: Dependency and impact data comes from the scip-neo4j MCP server. Use it before changing any existing symbol (function, class, method). symbol_id is the SCIP symbol string. To structure dependencies with the latest code, create a working branch and perform a Git commit and push for each set of tasks.
dependency_impact.tool: Call first on every symbol you intend to modify. STATUS: ALLOWED means go ahead. STATUS: LOCKED_CORE_THEORY means the symbol is an immutable core formula. Do not edit it. Follow the diagnostic_feedback and look for the cause in its callers instead.
Before changing a symbol's signature or behavior, list every transitive dependent (file_path, name). Review or update each one as part of the same task.
Use to understand call structure while debugging or planning (direction: upstream | downstream | both; max_depth defaults to 2).
dependency_impact.freshness: The graph reflects the last ingestion run, not the working tree. Symbols added or changed since then may be missing or stale. If a result looks wrong or empty, treat it as incomplete and fall back to reading the code. Do not assume the symbol is safe to change.
dependency_impact.unavailable: If the MCP server can't be reached, write that down as a blocker in the task's STATE.yaml entry. Continue only when you can confirm the change's scope by reading the code, and never modify code believed to be core theory without checking it.
dependency_impact.record: Add a one-line impact summary (dependents checked, any locked symbols found) to the task's result field.
